papers.title: Markov Chain Modelling for Mapping Customer Journeys on Instagram
papers.abstract: Understanding intricate user behavior on digital platforms, particularly social media like Instagram, is essential for strategic product optimization and targeted marketing. This paper presents a probabilistic methodology based on a Mixture of Markov Models (MOMM) and the Expectation-Maximization (EM) algorithm to automatically discover and summarize prototypical user sequences, or Customer Journey Maps (CJMs), from raw user event logs. We hypothesize that Instagram users are partitioned into K distinct behavioral clusters, each governed by a unique first-order Markov Chain. By optimizing the model parameters through Maximum Likelihood estimation, the EM algorithm efficiently extracts these K representative CJMs. This probabilistic framework offers significant advantages over traditional clustering methods, including requiring only a single input parameter (K) , robustly handling massive datasets (demonstrated scalability on over 7 million events for more than half a million customers) , and providing the capacity for dynamic, real-time prediction of a user's next most probable action.
